original.description: The User Management Service contract will encompass a comprehensive suite of offeringsdesigned to support and enhance user interactions and experience for ESA and Third PartyEO Missions.This service contract aims at integrating the User Communication and Information Portaltogether with the User Management functions, covered in the past by separate contracts,whereby ensuring autonomy to Industry in designing and using communication tools asadditional instrument to reach and stimulate a dynamic and variegated user community.The Information Portal is expected to provide seamless access to relevant content and data,Graphical and Editorial Servicesshall deliver visually engaging and professionally curatedmaterials, and finally User Experience Benchmarking Services enable performancecomparisons and insights. A dedicated User Help Desk completes the suite assisting userswith inquiries and technical support, ensuring prompt and effective resolution of issues.User Management Services will implement personalized access to tools, resources, andaccount features through the management of authorisation and authentication services withprovision of a secured User Area. The User Management service will foster a user-centricapproach that prioritizes accessibility, support, and continuous improvement driven by userfeedback.The User Management Service contract shall include the following services: Operations, maintenance and evolutions of the web services for data discoveryaccess and retrieval of Earth Observation products and information (composed byEarth Online, eoPortal, Swarm Data Handbook, EarthCARE Data Handbook, 3DVisuals and Quality Reports Advanced Search platforms). Content Management and Creation, including editorial and graphical services. Operations, maintenance and evolutions of an identity access management infrastructure with federated identity access configurations. Support to user community via a unique and integrated user help desk which serves as the single point of contact for answering to user enquiries and complaints, facilitating data access requests, monitoring and ensuring user satisfaction, and providing communications about system unavailability. The user help desk function will also provide AI powered chatbots and virtual support assistants being powered by a comprehensive and well-maintained and updated knowledgebase. Management of data access requests, assign authorisation to users for accessing restrained data, in agreement to applicable terms and condition (including quota management). Management of a large set of user profiles, including asecure and personalised self managementarea to access and manage account information, access settings and transaction history tracking support requests. By centralizing these functions, the userarea enhances convenience, engagement, and control, allowing users to efficiently interact with the system and AI powered virtual assistant while ensuring their dataand preferences are protected.  User experience benchmarking services for systematic analysing and monitoring of user and stakeholder feedback (surveys and behaviour analytics) and monitor performance to help identifying strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement

original.description: This tender covers the development of products and frameworks for users and stakeholders of Earth Observation (EO) services for climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction in Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. This tender is one of two being implemented as part of the 'Support to Disaster Risk Reduction through Earth Observation and Climate Services in South Asia' (SADRR) initiative (2026-2029). The initiative is being carried out in partnership with the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) and is funded by the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA) as part of the Global Gateway initiative.

original.description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity.  In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.
